references.text: Matthew's account of the Sermon on the Mount, where Jesus went up on a mountain, while Luke describes him standing on a level place – both passages introduce a major teaching address to the disciples and the crowd.

Large crowds followed Jesus from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and from the region across the Jordan, paralleling Luke's description of people coming from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and the coastal regions of Tyre and Sidon.
The preceding context where Jesus had spent the night in prayer on the mountain and chosen the twelve apostles before going down with them to the level place.

Mark describes that large crowds came to Jesus from Galilee, Judea, Jerusalem, Idumea, the region east of the Jordan, and from the areas around Tyre and Sidon – a very similar geographical listing as in Luke 6:17.
Here too it is mentioned that people had come from all the villages of Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem to hear Jesus, showing the same pattern of large crowds streaming in from throughout the region.
Jesus preached in the synagogues of Judea, demonstrating his ministry there which attracted the crowds mentioned in 6:17.
Large crowds followed Jesus, and he healed them all – a recurring theme that also prepares for the great gathering on the level place.
Jesus mentions Tyre and Sidon, the same pagan coastal cities referred to in Luke 6:17, showing that his reputation had reached these areas and people from there sought him out.
